notable.name: Juba Arabic
notable.note: widely used lingua franca, especially in the capital

language.note: Over 60 indigenous languages are spoken, mostly Nilo-Saharan; none has official status — English alone is the official working language
language.script: Latin (official use); no single script for the many indigenous languages

terrainDescription.zh: 地形以白尼羅河流域的沖積平原與稀樹草原為主，境內蘇德沼澤是世界最大的淡水濕地之一，與北方蘇丹的沙漠地形明顯不同。
terrainDescription.en: Dominated by White Nile floodplains and savanna, including the Sudd — one of the world's largest freshwater wetlands — in clear contrast to the desert terrain of Sudan to the north.

plate.color: black text on white background; standardized "SSD" country code adopted in November 2017

roadInfra.bollardStyle: No distinctively documented national style found — not a confirmed clue; Street View coverage is also sparse

utilityPole.transformerMount: Not independently documented for South Sudan specifically — flagging as unconfirmed rather than guessing a style

historicalContext.zh: 英語自2011年起為唯一官方語言，與蘇丹以阿拉伯語／英語雙官方語言的制度形成明顯對比；境內原住民語言逾60種，多屬尼羅-撒哈拉語系，朱巴阿拉伯語（一種以阿拉伯語為基礎的混合語）在首都地區廣泛作為溝通橋樑。
historicalContext.en: English has been the sole official language since 2011, a clear contrast with Sudan's Arabic/English co-official system. Over 60 indigenous languages are spoken, mostly Nilo-Saharan, with Juba Arabic (an Arabic-based pidgin) serving as a widespread lingua franca especially in the capital.
